title: Multi-source data integration through pooling and transfer learning improves generalizability and specialization of deep learning models for ICU mortality and length of stay prediction: a four-database external validation study
authors: Allyn J, Oliver M, Cerveau R, et al.
clinical_problem_outcome: In-ICU mortality and remaining length of stay (RLoS), predicted hourly from 5 h after admission
datasets: BlendedICU subsets: eICU-CRD, MIMIC-IV, AmsterdamUMCdb, HiRID
n_patients: 19,573 unique patients extracted per database (~80,000 total); training configs N=3,574 (AmsterdamUMC), 10,915 (MIMIC-IV), 14,489 (pooling/transfer)
n_hospitals_sites: 4 databases; eICU multicentre (N = 238 per Table 1); MIMIC-IV, AmsterdamUMC, HiRID single-centre
data_access: Open/credentialed (all four publicly available: PhysioNet / Amsterdam UMC Data Catalogue)
split_protocol: Random patient-level 70/15/15 split within each database; external = training on one database and testing on the others (leave-database-out); generalization tested on eICU+HiRID never seen in training
models: Temporal Pointwise Convolution (TPC); single-source vs data pooling vs transfer learning (pretrain MIMIC-IV, fine-tune AmsterdamUMC)
baselines: Transformer and LSTM benchmarked (Additional File 2, Table S2); single-source training as comparator for pooling/transfer
external_performance: Mortality AUROC (external, trained on given DB, tested on others): AmsterdamUMC 0.808; eICU 0.768; HiRID 0.777; MIMIC-IV 0.773. AUPRC: 0.294; 0.269; 0.331; 0.270. MAPE: 121.9; 100.1; 83.0; 109.5. Generalization (eICU+HiRID) AUROC: Amst-only 0.78, MIMIC-only 0.80, pooling 0.82; MAPE 117.08/117.41/111.07; Mcomposite 1.20/1.25/1.15
performance_source: Table 2 (internal vs external); Table 3 (training strategies); Fig. 2 (sample size)
internal_to_external_auroc_change: AmsterdamUMC +4.4%; eICU -2.5%; HiRID -8.7%; MIMIC-IV -13.8% (relative). AUPRC -3.3% to -40.8%; MAPE -0.3% to +51.8% (Table 2)
cis_seeds_repeats: 95% CIs: DeLong for AUROC; bootstrap (10,000 iterations) for MAPE/AUPRC; 1,000 bootstrap for Mcomposite. Seeds/repeated training runs: not reported
missing_data_handling: Forward-filling combined with missingness indicator masks (framed as MNAR); extreme values clipped to plausible ranges
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)
notes: Diagnoses excluded (not consistently available across DBs). Minimum ~15,000 training patients suggested for stable performance (Fig. 2). Random (not temporal) split acknowledged as limitation.

title: Continuous Evaluation Frameworks for Retrospective Evaluation of Clinical Machine Learning Models
authors: Natarajan A, Chang Y, McLaverty B, et al.
clinical_problem_outcome: Sepsis (Sepsis-3) continuous hourly prediction; proposes zone-based, predictive AMOC and notification-based continuous evaluation frameworks
n_patients: Emory 20,000 stays (1,142 sepsis, 5.7%); MIMIC-IV 58,694 ICU stays (5,531 sepsis, 9.4%)
split_protocol: Random stratified 70/30 train-test within each dataset; hyperparameters by 5-fold CV on hourly samples (authors note possible within-patient leakage across folds)
models: LightGBM regression (2019 PhysioNet challenge winner approach, retrained); XGBoost depth-1 model mimicking SIRS
baselines: SIRS-mimicking XGBoost; Epic sepsis model evaluation metrics (Wong et al.) as reporting template
internal_performance: Hospitalization-level AUROC: Emory LGBM 0.83, SIRS 0.74; MIMIC-IV LGBM 0.72, SIRS 0.68. 12-h time-horizon AUROC: Emory 0.80/0.75; MIMIC-IV 0.76/0.72. PPV Emory LGBM 0.23 (hosp level). Single time slice AUROC 1-6 h before onset in Fig. 4
cis_seeds_repeats: CIs for AUROC not reported; seeds not reported; challenge utility reproduced as 0.32 +/- 0.01 in double nested 5-fold CV on Emory
missing_data_handling: Forward filling within patient of 40 clinical variables, remaining missing set to NaN (LightGBM native handling), following challenge winner
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)
notes: Methodological paper on evaluation, not a new model. ICU hours used as input acknowledged as a bias.

title: Real-time machine learning model to predict short-term mortality in critically ill patients: development and international validation
authors: Lim L, Gim U, Cho K, et al.
datasets: SNUH internal cohort (5 ICUs, Seoul National University Hospital, 2007-2021); external: MIMIC-III, eICU-CRD, AmsterdamUMCdb
n_patients: Development 70,644 non-event + 983 event admissions; internal test 9,422 + 137; MIMIC-III 42,501 + 1,503; eICU-CRD 165,421 + 3,663; AmsterdamUMCdb 13,279 + 354 (307,907 admissions included overall)
n_hospitals_sites: Development: 1 hospital (5 ICUs); external: MIMIC-III 1, eICU-CRD 208 hospitals, AmsterdamUMCdb 1
data_access: Development private (available on request); external open/credentialed
split_protocol: Temporal split of internal data (train 2007-2018, tune 2019, test 2020-Oct 2021); external validation on full MIMIC-III, eICU-CRD, AmsterdamUMCdb
models: Ensemble of 3 LightGBM + 1 LSTM-based deep learning model (equal-weight averaging); transformer tried and excluded; temperature scaling
baselines: SPTTS, MEWS, NEWS, APACHE-II, SAPS, SOFA
external_performance: AUROC MIMIC-III 0.890 (0.889-0.891), eICU-CRD 0.886 (0.885-0.887), AmsterdamUMCdb 0.870 (0.868-0.873); NEWS 0.746/0.798/0.819. ECE 0.205/0.199/0.254 (NEWS 0.249/0.197/0.309). AUPRC in Additional file Table E6 (not in main text)
performance_source: Abstract; Results text; Fig. 1; Additional file Table E6, Fig. E8 (ECE)
calibration_reported: Yes (ECE; calibration in Additional file Fig. E8)
cis_seeds_repeats: 95% CIs for AUROC; seeds/repeats not reported
missing_data_handling: Median imputation when initial admission value missing; otherwise forward filling; out-of-range values set to missing; standardization with training statistics
missingness_indicators_used: No explicit indicators; time-delta features (time since last vital sign / last lab / ICU admission) included
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)
notes: Abstract says 'MIMIC'; Methods specify MIMIC-III. Under-sampling of non-events per epoch.

title: Development and validation of a dynamic early warning system with time-varying machine learning models for predicting hemodynamic instability in critical care: a multicohort study
authors: Chiang DH, Jiang Z, Tian C, et al.
clinical_problem_outcome: Hemodynamic instability (first intervention segment: vasoactive/inotropes, fluids, packed red cells) after 6 h in ICU; TvHEWS with 24 hourly models
datasets: VGHTPE 2010 cohort (Taipei Veterans General Hospital, 2010-2021); VGHTPE 2022 cohort (Jan-Jun 2022); MIMIC-IV
n_patients: VGHTPE 2010: 18,438 patients (3,671 unstable); VGHTPE 2022: 700 (150 unstable); MIMIC-IV: 47,492 (5,475 unstable)
data_access: Development private (on request with agreements); MIMIC-IV open/credentialed
split_protocol: VGHTPE 2010 split train/validation/test 2:2:1 with 5-fold CV; temporal same-site validation (VGHTPE 2022); external MIMIC-IV
models: 24 time-varying XGBoost classifiers (1-24 h before intervention) + alarm rule (alpha = share of 24 outputs >0.5)
baselines: not reported (no clinical score comparator in main text)
internal_performance: TvHEWS AUROC 0.93, AUPRC 0.82 (VGHTPE 2010); single-hour models median AUROC 0.91 (95% CI 0.91-0.92); Brier 0.082
external_performance: VGHTPE 2022: AUROC 0.92, AUPRC 0.79, Brier 0.085. MIMIC-IV: AUROC 0.82, AUPRC 0.61, Brier 0.116; precision 0.723 / recall 0.362 at alpha 65%; missed alarm rate 0.638
cis_seeds_repeats: 95% CI only for median per-hour metrics; seeds not reported
missing_data_handling: 'Nonrandom missingness strategy': latest available value within variable-specific forward windows (e.g., 2 h HR, 26 h labs); NIBP substituted for missing invasive BP; FiO2 set to 21% if unspecified; outliers set to null; models run without imputation (XGBoost); variables >60% missing excluded
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)
notes: Alpha threshold re-optimized per cohort (35% optimal for MIMIC-IV). Procalcitonin unavailable in MIMIC-IV (45 of 46 variables). Two authors employed by Philips.

title: Prioritising deteriorating patients using time-to-event analysis: prediction model development and internal-external validation
authors: Blythe R, Parsons R, Barnett AG, et al.
setting_population: Adult acute-care inpatients on wards (ICU admissions/time excluded)
clinical_problem_outcome: Time to in-hospital mortality (clinical deterioration), ranking patients by risk
datasets: Routinely collected vital signs/admin data, 5 Australian hospitals (2019-2020)
split_protocol: Internal-external cross-validation by hospital (leave-one-hospital-out, 5 folds); imputation repeated within CV using only prediction-time variables
models: Cox regression with time-varying covariates, restricted cubic splines
baselines: Discrete-time logistic regression (death within 24 h) with same covariates
internal_performance: Cross-validated (held-out hospital mean) Uno time-dependent AUC: Cox 0.97 at 12 h, 0.96 at 24 h, 0.93 at 1 week; logistic 0.93 at 12/24 h, 0.88 at 1 week
external_performance: Same as left (all estimates are on held-out hospitals); per-hospital AUC values in supplement
internal_to_external_auroc_change: not applicable (only internal-external estimates reported in main text)
calibration_reported: Yes (smoothed calibration curves per hospital; risk generally overestimated, varied by hospital)
cis_seeds_repeats: Mean and range across hospitals; CIs not reported in main text; seeds not reported
missing_data_handling: Single random-forest imputation (R missRanger) with predictive mean matching (>=3 candidates); summary features over prior 24 h used as imputation predictors; CV imputation excluded outcome information
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)
notes: Statistical (non-ML) model; non-ICU ward population. Missingness: temperature 28.3%, pulse 20.3%, etc.

title: Development and external validation of a machine learning model for the prediction of persistent acute kidney injury stage 3 in multi-centric, multi-national intensive care cohorts
authors: Zappala S, Alfieri F, Ancona A, et al.
setting_population: Adult ICU stays with AKI stage 2-3
clinical_problem_outcome: Persistent AKI stage 3 (>=72 h, or >=48 h with death, or RRT after >24 h stage 3), real-time
datasets: Development: MIMIC-III + AmsterdamUMCdb; external: eICU-CRD, MargheritaTre (GiViTI, Italy)
n_patients: 7,759 ICU patients: AmsterdamUMCdb 1,607 stays; MIMIC-III 1,497; eICU 3,562; MargheritaTre 1,093
n_hospitals_sites: Development 2 single-centre DBs; eICU 139 centres; MargheritaTre 16 centres
data_access: MIMIC-III, AmsterdamUMCdb, eICU open/credentialed; MargheritaTre on request (third party)
split_protocol: Random 70/30 split of MIMIC-III + AmsterdamUMCdb stays (train / threshold-calibration + internal validation); external eICU and MargheritaTre
models: Gradient boosted trees (explainable tree regressor), 542 features, SHAP
external_performance: auROC eICU 93.58 [92.37-94.85]; MargheritaTre 85.29 [83.17-87.54]; auPR 44.57 and 49.78. Creatinine-only baseline: auROC 0.91 eICU, 0.83 MargheritaTre
internal_to_external_auroc_change: Internal 0.90/0.93 -> eICU 0.94 (no drop) and MargheritaTre 0.85 (drop of 0.05-0.08)
calibration_reported: No calibration curve/statistic (only threshold 'calibration' at 80% sensitivity)
cis_seeds_repeats: Table 2 reports IQR for auROC/auPR (abstract labels them 95% CI); seeds not reported
missing_data_handling: Hourly resampling with variable-specific validity durations (Max_gap); variables measured in >70% of stays used; features include time since last measurement and boolean absence indicator per variable (except creatinine, diuresis)
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)
notes: MargheritaTre deliberately used to test robustness to high missingness. Fairness (AOD) analysis.

title: Interpretable machine learning model for new-onset atrial fibrillation prediction in critically ill patients: a multi-center study
authors: Guan C, Gong A, Zhao Y, et al.
setting_population: Adult non-cardiac-surgery ICU patients (>2 days ICU)
clinical_problem_outcome: New-onset atrial fibrillation after first ICU day
n_hospitals_sites: 1 hospital (BIDMC) for both cohorts (non-overlapping time periods)
split_protocol: Undersampling; 5-fold CV split into training/internal validation; 10-fold CV for tuning; external = earlier-era MIMIC-III (temporal, same hospital)
external_validation: Yes - but same hospital, different era (temporal)
models: XGBoost (best), SVM, AdaBoost, MLP, NN, NB, LR, GBM; LASSO feature selection (23 vars)
performance_source: Results text; Fig. 3; Table 2; Fig. S2 (external ROC)
cis_seeds_repeats: 95% CIs for AUC; seeds not reported
missing_data_handling: KNNImputer for variables with <20% missing; variables >20% missing discarded
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)
notes: CI for internal AUC inconsistent between abstract and results. Title says multi-center though both datasets from BIDMC.

title: Interpretable machine learning models for predicting venous thromboembolism in the intensive care unit: an analysis based on data from 207 centers
authors: Guan C, Ma F, Chang S, et al.
setting_population: Adult ICU patients (first admission, stay >=24 h)
clinical_problem_outcome: New VTE (DVT/PE) during ICU stay, using first-24-h data
n_hospitals_sites: eICU multicentre (title: 207 centers); hospitals randomly allocated ~70/30
split_protocol: By hospital: randomly selected hospitals containing ~70% of patients for training, remaining hospitals (~30%) for validation; 5-fold CV random search for tuning
external_validation: Hospital-level held-out split within eICU (described by authors as external validation)
models: Random forest (final), XGBoost, SVM; stepwise logistic regression feature selection (24 vars); DALEX
baselines: not reported (ML models compared to each other)
external_performance: Held-out hospitals (Table 2; set not explicitly labelled): RF AUC 0.9378, accuracy 0.9958, kappa 0.8371, F1 0.8393, sens 0.7791, spec 0.9989; XGBoost AUC 0.9492; SVM AUC 0.8290 (threshold 0.2)
missing_data_handling: Multiple imputation ('multiple interpolation'); patients with >30% missing data excluded
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)
notes: Accuracy close to no-information rate (0.9858) due to 1.5% prevalence; AUPRC not reported.

title: Development and validation of the creatinine clearance predictor machine learning models in critically ill adults
authors: Huang CY, Guiza F, Wouters P, et al.
setting_population: Adult ICU patients without prior KRT
datasets: EPaNIC RCT database (development); M@tric database, University Hospitals Leuven 2013-2018 (external)
n_patients: Development 2,825 patients (18,494 patient-days); external 9,576 patients (53,943 patient-days)
n_hospitals_sites: EPaNIC described as multicenter (number of centres not stated in main text); external 1 hospital (Leuven)
split_protocol: Internal 10-fold CV on EPaNIC; external validation on later M@tric Leuven cohort
models: Gradient boosting regressor (Core; Core+BGA; Core+BGA+Monitoring), Optuna tuning
baselines: Prediction day's CrCl carried forward (current practice)
internal_performance: Reported only in Additional file 1 (Figs. S2-S3, Table S1) - not in main text
external_performance: All days: Core+BGA+Monitoring MAE 18.1 (17.9-18.3) ml/min, RMSE 28.9 (28-29.7); Core MAE 18.5, RMSE 29; reference MAE 20.6 (20.3-20.9), RMSE 40.1 (37.9-42.3). Unstable days: Core MAE 34.8, RMSE 47.3 vs reference 50.1/71.1. Stable days: model RMSE 13.9 vs reference 9.3
internal_to_external_auroc_change: not applicable (regression; internal results in supplement only)
calibration_reported: No formal calibration (predicted vs actual scatter with lowess, Fig. 3)
cis_seeds_repeats: 95% CIs for MAE/RMSE; Diebold-Mariano tests; seeds not reported
missing_data_handling: Features with >10% missing excluded; remaining imputed with mean (continuous) / mode (categorical) from development cohort
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)

title: Beyond binary AKI classification: development and external validation of a distributional model predicting serum creatinine and urine output trajectories in ICU patients
authors: Jonkers J, Rouze A, Verhaeghe J, et al.
setting_population: Adult ICU stays >=48 h without CKD/prior KRT
clinical_problem_outcome: Distributions of future sCr (24/48 h) and urine output (6-48 h); derived KDIGO stage 1-3 and persistent stage 3 AKI risk
datasets: MIMIC-IV v3.1 (training/temporal test); UZGent (Ghent); eICU-CRD; AmsterdamUMCdb
n_patients: Train 4,118 (2011-2013), validation 4,128 (2014-2016), temporal test 3,838 (2017-2019); UZGent 4,442; eICU 10,760; AmsterdamUMC 6,129 ICU stays
n_hospitals_sites: MIMIC-IV 1; UZGent 1; eICU multicentre (number not stated); AmsterdamUMC 1
data_access: MIMIC-IV, eICU, AmsterdamUMCdb open/credentialed; UZGent private
split_protocol: Temporal split of MIMIC-IV by admission year; external validation on UZGent, eICU, AmsterdamUMC
models: NGBoost multivariate distributional regression (default hyperparameters, early stopping)
baselines: Gradient boosting tree classifiers per KDIGO stage
internal_performance: Temporal MIMIC-IV, 24-h stage 3: AUROC 0.948 (classifier 0.942), AUPRC 0.672 (0.641), Brier 0.035, ECE 0.005
external_performance: 24-h stage 3: UZGent AUROC 0.984, AUPRC 0.771, Brier 0.012, ECE 0.002; eICU 0.969 / 0.804 / 0.025 / 0.008; AmsterdamUMC 0.988 / 0.877 / 0.015 / 0.005. Mean AUPRC all stages 0.774 (abstract). Persistent stage 3: AUROC 0.825-0.889
internal_to_external_auroc_change: No drop: temporal 0.948 -> external 0.969-0.988 (prevalence differs: 6.7% vs 2.8-6.3%)
cis_seeds_repeats: No CIs in Table 2; seeds not reported
missing_data_handling: Not described in main text (72-h window summary statistics; implausible values excluded; sCr linearly interpolated for labels)
verification_status: VERIFIED (full text read via Europe PMC)
notes: Only 5-27% of ICU stays retained after filtering. Robustness to alternative baseline-sCr definition shown without retraining.

title: Mortality and antibiotic timing in deep learning-derived surviving sepsis campaign risk groups: a multicenter study

models: COMPOSER (sepsis), Shock-Net (transformer) for shock; multivariable logistic regression for outcome associations

notes: ED rather than ICU; primary aim is antibiotic-timing association, not model development. Authors hold equity in related startup.

title: ORAKLE: Optimal Risk prediction for mAke30 in patients with sepsis associated AKI using deep LEarning
authors: Oh W, Veshtaj M, Sawant A, et al.

models: ORAKLE: Dynamic DeepHit (3 LSTM layers x100 + 3 FC layers)

performance_source: Abstract; Results text; Figs. 2, 4-6; Suppl. Tables S4-S6
cis_seeds_repeats: 95% CIs by 10,000 bootstrap; seeds not reported

notes: Some printed C-index CIs do not contain point estimate (e.g., 0.77 (0.79-0.81) SICdb) - as printed.

title: Development and external validation of age-specific predictive models for sepsis in critically ill neonates and children using multidimensional hematological parameters: a multicenter retrospective study

title: Machine learning models compared with current clinical indices to predict the outcome of high flow nasal cannula therapy in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure

title: A prediction model for 'ICU mortality or prolonged ICU stay' in critically unwell patients with acute pancreatitis: insights from a 2003-2020 cohort analysis using the ANZICS-CORE database
authors: Venkatesh K, Schlub TE, Barreto SG, et al.
setting_population: Adult ICU patients with acute pancreatitis (first ICU admission)
clinical_problem_outcome: High-risk trajectory: ICU death or ICU LOS >7 days, from first-24-h data
n_patients: 13,275 included; Model 1 n=5,882 (complete cases); Model 2 n=542 (2017 onwards)

internal_performance: Model 1: AUROC 82.3, accuracy 77.7%, kappa 0.446. Model 2: AUROC 82.7 (Table 2; text 0.829, Fig. 2 0.827), accuracy 79.5%, kappa 0.490, sens 53.9%, spec 91.6%, Brier 0.148

notes: Statistical model, not ML. AUROC reported inconsistently (82.7 / 0.829 / 0.827).
